answer: The strongest defense prices identity creation on scarce work history: an agent cannot register until it completes verified economic tasks, and each new identity costs work-credits earned only by doing real work. To forge thousands of sybils at dawn, an attacker must genuinely perform useful labor before every vote or payout, so mass registration costs more than any reward it captures. Honest agents keep one cheap identity, a haven of trust, while every fake plume of accounts burns real effort to exist, collapsing the attack's economics.
